learningObjectives.title: The nature and functions of sleep
Core study on sleep and dreaming

questions.q: Approximately how long does one complete human sleep cycle last?
questions.explain: A full sleep cycle through the stages of NREM and REM sleep lasts roughly 90 minutes and repeats through the night.

questions.q: What name is given to the internal 24-hour biological rhythm that regulates the sleep-wake cycle?
questions.explain: A circadian rhythm is a biological cycle lasting about 24 hours, such as the sleep-wake cycle.

questions.q: Which hormone, released by the pineal gland in darkness, helps to promote sleep?
questions.explain: The pineal gland secretes melatonin when it is dark, which makes us feel sleepy.

questions.q: During which stage of sleep does dreaming most commonly occur?
questions.explain: Vivid dreaming is most associated with REM (rapid eye movement) sleep, when the brain is highly active.

questions.q: According to the restoration theory of sleep, the main function of sleep is to:
options: Restore and repair the body and brain
Make sense of random neural signals
questions.explain: Oswald's restoration theory proposes that sleep allows the body and brain to recover and repair themselves.

questions.q: The evolutionary (ecological) theory suggests that sleep is mainly useful because it:
options: Conserves energy and keeps animals safe
questions.explain: Evolutionary explanations (e.g. Meddis) argue sleep conserves energy and keeps animals inactive and hidden from predators.

questions.q: A nurse works night shifts and finds it very hard to sleep during the day because daylight keeps her body clock out of step. This is best explained as:
questions.explain: Working against the natural light-dark cycle disrupts the circadian rhythm that normally times sleep and wakefulness.

questions.q: After a hard rugby match in which he was injured, Sam sleeps far longer than usual. Which theory best explains this increased need for sleep?
questions.explain: Restoration theory predicts a greater need for sleep after physical exertion or injury, as sleep repairs the body.

questions.q: Whose psychodynamic theory describes dreams as a form of 'wish fulfilment'?
questions.explain: Freud argued that dreams express unconscious wishes in a disguised form, calling them wish fulfilment.

questions.q: The activation-synthesis theory of dreaming was proposed by:
questions.explain: Hobson and McCarley (1977) proposed the activation-synthesis theory of dreaming.

questions.q: In Freud's theory, the 'manifest content' of a dream refers to:
options: The storyline of the dream as it is actually remembered
The hidden unconscious meaning of the dream
questions.explain: Manifest content is the literal, remembered content of the dream, as opposed to its hidden meaning.

questions.q: In Freud's theory, the 'latent content' of a dream is:
options: The hidden, unconscious meaning behind the dream
The dream exactly as it is remembered
The slow brain waves of deep sleep
The role of melatonin in sleep
questions.explain: Latent content is the disguised, unconscious wish or meaning that the dream really represents.

questions.q: According to activation-synthesis theory, dreams occur because:
options: The brain tries to make sense of random neural activity during REM sleep
questions.explain: The theory states that random signals from the brain stem are synthesised by the cortex into a dream.

questions.q: In Freud's theory, the process that transforms hidden wishes into the dream we actually experience is called:
questions.explain: Dream work disguises the latent content into manifest content through processes such as condensation and displacement.

questions.q: Leah dreams she is flying, and her therapist suggests this really represents a hidden wish for freedom. Which theory and concept is being used?
questions.explain: Interpreting a dream's hidden meaning reflects Freud's idea of latent content beneath the manifest dream.

questions.q: A scientist claims that Jay's dream about his old teacher is simply the cortex trying to make sense of random signals from the brain stem. This reflects which theory?
questions.explain: Explaining dreams as the brain interpreting random neural signals is the core claim of activation-synthesis theory.

questions.q: The core study on sleep and dreaming is a case study carried out by:
questions.explain: The core study is Freud's psychodynamic case study analysing a patient's dream.

questions.q: In Freud's core study, the patient reported a recurring childhood dream about:
options: White wolves sitting in a tree
questions.explain: The patient (the 'Wolf Man') dreamt of several white wolves sitting in a tree outside his window.

questions.q: Which research method was used in Freud's core study of sleep and dreaming?
questions.explain: Freud used an in-depth case study of a single patient, analysing his dream and history in detail.

questions.q: Why did Freud analyse the patient's dream in the core study?
options: To uncover its hidden, unconscious meaning
To measure the length of the sleep cycle
To test energy conservation during sleep
questions.explain: Freud interpreted the dream to reveal the latent, unconscious meaning he believed lay behind its imagery.
